 Nestlé Malaysia, Red Crescent prepare 7,000 flood aid packs ahead of monsoon
 TheStar 
 Sun, Nov 01, 2026 03:50pm - 7 hours 
 View Original 
 [Third from left] YTM Tan Sri Tunku Puteri Intan Safinaz binti Almarhum Sultan Abdul Halim Mu’adzam Shah, National Chairperson of the Malaysian Red Crescent (MRC), and [third from right] Juan Aranols, Chief Executive Officer of Nestlé Malaysia, joined by [from right] Tengku Ida Adura Tengku Ismail, Executive Director, Legal & Secretarial, Nestlé Malaysia, and Raja Nurmaria Murni Raja Nur Azmi, Executive Director of Group Corporate Affairs, Nestlé Malaysia & Singapore, alongside MRC representatives, Dato’ Danial Iskandar bin Abdul Rahman, MRC Secretary General and Lee Shy Jing Chairperson MRC Negeri Sembilan, mark Nestlé Malaysia’s contribution of RM1.8 million in products-in-kind and financial support towards the overall flood relief initiative for the 2026 monsoon season. KUALA LUMPUR: Nestlé Malaysia and the Malaysian Red Crescent (MRC) have prepared 7,000 food and nutrition aid packs for families at risk of flooding during the monsoon season.
 The supplies are being transported to Kedah, Kelantan, Pahang and Terengganu as part of flood preparedness efforts.
 In Sabah, 40 volunteers from Nestlé’s local operations, Harrisons Sabah and MRC Sabah have prepared 1,000 aid bags for distribution within the state.
 Nestlé Malaysia said its contribution of products and financial assistance for this year’s initiative was valued at about RM1.8mil. 
 ...
 Summary Overview 
 • Nestlé Malaysia and the Malaysian Red Crescent (MRC) have prepared 7,000 food and nutrition aid packs for the 2026 monsoon season, with supplies being pre-positioned in Kedah, Kelantan, Pahang, and Terengganu to ensure rapid deployment.
• The initiative represents a RM1.8 million contribution in products and financial support, marking the fourth consecutive year of this partnership which has cumulatively assisted over 30,000 flood-affected families since 2023.
• An additional 1,000 aid bags have been prepared in Sabah by 40 volunteers from Harrisons Sabah and MRC Sabah, while 400 Nestlé employees nationwide participated in the packing exercises alongside university and community representatives.
• Company leadership emphasized that early preparation is critical for humanitarian effectiveness, with MRC chairperson Tan Sri Tunku Puteri Intan Safinaz noting that pre-positioning supplies allows for more efficient mobilization when disasters strike.
• Beyond the main initiative, Nestlé Malaysia collaborated with Yayasan Food Bank Malaysia to distribute 800 additional aid packs to remote communities in Tumpat and Jeli, Kelantan, with support from the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA).
